The input beads-1.csv hashes to 02cf52d4...9051 and the vendored ArchaeoPhases tarball to 728a0d0c...a801, both as planned. The plan hash 7ff05a24... matches plan-approval.json and gate-report.json.

Reproduced values in the report trace to raw outputs. For example, the section 7 unrounded matrix gives Cowrie-Disc 0.999667, Amethyst-Disc 0.867167, and Amber-Amethyst/Cowrie 1. compare.R reads published values from published-values.csv and holds only figure readings inline, with no hard-coded reproduced values.

Weaker spots: the visual judgements for T03, T04, T21, and T23 were made against 200-400 dpi renders kept only in scratch, and the Fig 6 pixel measurements are encoded in compare.R without the render, so they cannot be re-checked from the artefacts alone. '--network none' is asserted in log.md and environment.md, but no artefact captures the docker run command line.

Published Supplement Tables 2-10 (54 cells), the section 10.1-10.9 text ranges, section 11 (Dghnt(e)Dghnt = 1), section 12 (poDd; overlaps 0.73), and paper p.16 l.376 (0.87) were checked against pdftotext of the corpus PDFs. All are transcribed correctly in the report.

The Supp Fig 2 bar heights, read from the rendered page 49, are 20, 4, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 1, 1, and 12, as the plan and compare.R state. Recomputing from T22-54-relations.csv gives 19, 5, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 1, 1, 12 unrounded and 20, 4, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 1, 1, 12 at 2 dp (right-closed), as reported.
T09 recomputed: 54 relations, 2-dp median 0.375, 20 at or below 0.10, and 12 above 0.9, all involving BE1-Disc. This matches the report.

comparison.json sums to 276 values compared and 273 matched, as the report states. The outcome tally is 24 EXACT_MATCH, 1 WITHIN_PRECISION, 5 MINOR, 3 CANNOT_COMPARE, and 1 PAPER_ERROR, giving 25/34 = 0.7353, consistent with gate-report.json.

Precision masking was checked. The report lists unrounded values next to the 2-dp values for every matrix cell. T34's WITHIN_PRECISION (0.725 against a published 0.73, where R's round() gives 0.72) is disclosed openly and fits the instrument's 'within rounding of reported precision' definition.

comparison.json covers all 34 locked target ids (T01-T34), and none was dropped. T10 and T11 stay in the denominator as expected-untestable under R2, with documented 404 re-probes. The paper Fig 1 and Fig 5 exclusions were approved in plan-approval.json.

The enumeration was checked independently: the paper has Figures 1-6 and no tables, and the supplement has Figures 1-3 and Tables 1-10. A grep of the main text for numeric result statements found only 0.87 (T06) and the '54 relations' statement (T09). The 'negligible between-run variability' claim (p.11 l.272-273) is folded into T10 as planned.

T02 was attempted and its failure documented: section-status.csv records 'undefined columns selected', and the index check shows max index 78 against 77 columns. It was not silently omitted. The section 10.5 'nine' versus 'six' inconsistency is recorded as a finding, per the approver's ruling.

T06 is classed PAPER_ERROR, but the instrument's criterion is that 'the paper's own tabulated data supports the reproduced value'. No paper or supplement table reports the section 7 oFD matrix. The call rests on circumstantial evidence: 0.87 equals the neighbouring Amethyst(oFD)Disc cell (0.86717), and the other 54 table values match. That is persuasive, but it is not the instrument's verification test. Read strictly, the outcome is MAJOR_DISCREPANCY (|diff| 0.13) pending human confirmation. Coverage is unaffected because PAPER_ERROR is not counted as reproduced, and the call is escalated.

T04 placement differences of up to 47 years (Disc lower box) are counted as 'within a few decades' (MINOR). The comparison uses an invented convention (bar position +22 years against reproduced first and last event years) for a figure whose placement rule is unpublished. That is defensible for a hand-drawn figure but is a generous reading.

The T23 left panel ({p}) is 'reproduced' by choosing allen_illustrate('transform'), whose output is {p}, and attaching the published title. The left panel is the expected relation, an input, so its 13 memberships matched by construction, which inflates the 26/26 count. T01's 78/78 is likewise the package drawing its own analytic definitions. I verified that the opaque sets in paper Fig 2 match.

Under T03 the report says BE1-Disc runs '665 to 756, the later 7th to mid-8th century' and treats this as confirming the text's 'second half of the seventh century and the early eighth century'. The figure itself does match the published figure visually (I checked), so the MINOR outcome stands, but the text-agreement claim is slightly stretched.

The T02 failure may be caused by the environment version rather than the published materials. The ArchaeoPhases 1.8 read_oxcal source (ImportCSV.R) drops the 'Pass' column and the empty trailing column, leaving 77 of 79. In raw CSV (Pass-inclusive) numbering, the authors' indices c(3:5, 7, 9, 12:78) select exactly 72 contexts and exclude exactly 5, matching the 72 interments in paper Fig 3. In 1.8 numbering they overflow, and 12:77 would also drop BuD391A and BuD391B together. This strongly suggests the authors' read_oxcal kept the iteration column (an earlier or development ArchaeoPhases), or that they indexed raw CSV columns. In 1.8, x_min/x_max also become ggplot2::xlim(500, 700), which would clip the published 400-800 axis, again pointing to a different version.

environment.md says ArchaeoPhases 1.8 is 'the only CRAN release that exports every function the supplement calls'. The vendored package's own NEWS shows allen_observe_frequency, allen_illustrate, and allen_observe were added in 1.6, and read_oxcal and occurrence_plot in 1.5. The claim is therefore unsupported, and no alternative release was examined. The comparison report's statement that 'the published figure therefore cannot have come from the published code and data as given' overstates the case: it holds only under ArchaeoPhases 1.8.

Otherwise the method is sound. A diff of section 10.4 confirms the edits are path-only. Section 6 was moved after sections 7-10; this is documented and harmless, because those blocks only read bead_list and re-read the MCMC file. The aids live in a separate R1-labelled script that calls documented exports only. Duplicate labels in BE1.Melon and BE1.Koch20Ye come from the authors' own list construction (sections 5.25 and 5.32), not from transcription, which the exact table matches corroborate.

Process note: log.md finding 5 self-reports a host directory listing of .claude/skills/reproduction-assessor/references/ that showed the names of two blinded entries. It says nothing was opened. This bears on run blinding and needs human adjudication, though it does not touch any reproduced value.

verdict_challenge.rationale: PARTIAL is supported. Fifty-four of 54 supplement table cells, all ordinal inferences (T07 and T08), and the tempo-plot figure reproduce from the authors' code and archived MCMC output in a pinned Docker environment. However, T10 and T11 (Supplement Table 1 and the main-text replicability claim) cannot be tested because four of the five MCMC runs are unpublished (404). That alone rules out SUCCESSFUL under the instrument's data-unavailability rule. Nothing supports FAILED: every substantive conclusion checked is confirmed. My two concerns go to target-level attribution, not to the overall verdict. T02's CANNOT_COMPARE may be an artefact of the ArchaeoPhases 1.8 choice (an off-by-one in read_oxcal column handling), not a defect in the published materials. T06's PAPER_ERROR rests on circumstantial evidence rather than the instrument's tabulated-data test. Even if T02 were recovered with a different package version, T10 and T11 would keep the verdict at PARTIAL.

recommendations: Reword the T02 attribution in the comparison report and comparison.json. 'The published figure cannot have come from the published code and data' should be qualified as holding only under ArchaeoPhases 1.8. Record the evidence that the authors' indices fit Pass-inclusive numbering, which would select exactly 72 contexts.

Correct environment.md's claim that 1.8 is the only CRAN release exporting the needed functions; the package NEWS shows they arrived in 1.6 and 1.5. Ask the registrant whether a follow-up should test T02 under an earlier ArchaeoPhases release (an environment change, not an analysis change) before T02's CANNOT_COMPARE enters study data.

Have a human adjudicate T06. Either accept PAPER_ERROR on the circumstantial evidence, noting that the instrument's tabulated-data criterion is not literally met, or reclassify it MAJOR_DISCREPANCY pending author contact. Either way coverage stays 25/34.
Note in the report that the T23 left panel and the T01 lattices match by construction (analytic package illustrations), so their membership counts are weak evidence.

Keep the page renders used for the visual and placement comparisons (T03, T04, T21, and T23) inside the attempt directory, and log the exact docker run command line, so that these judgements can be re-checked from the artefacts.
Have a human adjudicate the executor's self-reported directory listing that exposed two blinded entry names (log.md finding 5) under the run's blinding rules.
